grants.title: Urban and Community Forestry Grant Program, Round 17 — tree inventories and management plans
grants.summary: Ten million dollars statewide for street and park tree inventories, assessments, and community forest management plans. Projects must sit on public property, private land open to the public, or recognized Tribal reservation land. Applications go through the Statewide Financial System; nonprofits must prequalify before the deadline.

applicant_notes.state_agency: Not named in the eligibility list for this round.
applicant_notes.for_profit: Not eligible as applicant; may be retained as a contractor.
applicant_notes.individual: Not eligible.

geography.notes: Statewide, subject to the eligible geographic boundaries defined in the Request for Applications.

requirements: Applicant must be registered in the Statewide Financial System (SFS)
Not-for-profits must complete NYS prequalification before the deadline
Project site must be public property, private land open to the public, or recognized Tribal reservation land
One application per applicant
grants.verification_note: Total pool ($10M) and deadline confirmed. Per-project award floor and ceiling were not stated in the sources checked — read the RFA before entering numbers.

grants.title: Advancing Forest Markets — Tree Market Boost and Revitalization
grants.summary: New program with $46 million available to expand seedling supply and forest-product capacity. The Tree Market Boost track funds forestry and forest-product businesses and other entities working on reforestation, forest management, low-grade wood products, timber and maple. No match required, and awards carry a participation incentive payment on contract execution. Funding cannot be used to break ground or disturb site vegetation.

applicant_notes.individual: Individual private landowners are named as eligible, subject to USDA enrollment requirements.
applicant_notes.for_profit: Forestry and forest-product businesses are a primary target of this track.

requirements: Applications submitted through the Statewide Financial System (SFS)
All funded work must be completed before January 2028
Funds may not be used for direct implementation that breaks ground or disturbs site vegetation
Participation incentive payment of $2,000-$10,000 depending on project size
grants.verification_note: Tagged native_plants on the basis of the programme's stated aim of increasing access to high-quality, locally grown seedlings for reforestation, afforestation and climate resilience. The notice does not use the word "native" — confirm species requirements in the guidelines.

grants.title: Climate Smart Communities Grant Program — 2026 round
grants.summary: Eighteen million dollars for municipal climate mitigation and adaptation. About $17 million funds implementation projects from $35,000 to $2 million; a separate $1 million funds planning, inventory and assessment projects from $10,000 to $200,000. Named eligible topics include reducing emissions from food waste, flood risk reduction, refrigerant management and smart growth analysis. The 2026 round closed on 31 July; the CFA cycle historically runs May to July each year.

applicant_notes.state_agency: Not eligible. Program is for local governments.
applicant_notes.nonprofit: Not eligible as lead applicant; can participate as a project partner.
applicant_notes.for_profit: Not eligible as applicant; may be retained as a vendor.
applicant_notes.individual: Not eligible.

geography.notes: Statewide. Eligibility expanded effective April 2026 to include local public authorities, public benefit corporations and Indian Nations.

requirements: Applications accepted only through the NYS Consolidated Funding Application (CFA)
Local match of 50% of total project cost for most projects
Match may drop to 20% for financial-hardship communities or projects in disadvantaged communities
Applicant must be registered in the SFS Grants Management System
Grantee must own the project site or hold a climate change mitigation easement
grants.verification_note: Next round expected to open in the May-July 2027 CFA cycle; dates not yet published.

grants.title: NYS Consolidated Funding Application — 2026 round
grants.funder: Empire State Development / Regional Economic Development Councils
grants.summary: The single application portal for more than 20 state programs across eight agencies, including most DEC and EFC environmental grants. Up to $60 million in Regional Council Capital Funds plus program-specific money. Deadline-enforced programs closed 31 July 2026 at 4pm; open-enrollment programs inside the CFA keep accepting applications until their funds run out.

applicant_notes.individual: Not an applicant category; individual projects must go through an eligible entity.
applicant_notes.state_agency: State agencies administer rather than apply.

geography.notes: The Finger Lakes REDC covers Genesee, Livingston, Monroe, Ontario, Orleans, Seneca, Wayne, Wyoming and Yates. The Western New York REDC covers Allegany, Cattaraugus, Chautauqua, Erie and Niagara.

requirements: Regional Councils score projects on alignment with the regional strategic plan
Open-enrollment programs within the CFA are not subject to the July deadline
grants.verification_note: This is a portal record, not a grant. It exists so the app can explain why a cluster of state deadlines all land on the same date.

grants.title: Clean Energy Communities Program, Round 3.0 — action and designation grants
grants.summary: Municipalities earn points by completing high-impact clean energy actions, then draw grant funding to implement further projects. Action grants run up to $290,000 for large municipalities and up to $97,500 for small and medium ones. Submissions of new high-impact actions have been paused since November 2024, but designated communities can still submit grant project applications on a rolling basis.

applicant_notes.nonprofit: Not an applicant; municipalities apply.
applicant_notes.for_profit: Not an applicant.
applicant_notes.individual: Not an applicant.

geography.notes: Any New York county, city, town or village. Additional support for projects in disadvantaged communities.

requirements: Municipality must hold Clean Energy Communities designation to access action grants
High-impact action submissions have been closed since 7 November 2024
Custom, pre-approved and direct-to-voucher proposal routes are available
grants.verification_note: The $290,000 / $97,500 tiers were published before the October 2024 step-down in funding levels. Confirm current tier amounts with a NYSERDA CEC coordinator before budgeting.

grants.title: Community Climate Action Fund Pilot Program
grants.funder: Monroe County Department of Environmental Services
grants.summary: Monroe County's first direct climate grant to its own municipalities. Individual municipalities can receive up to $10,000 in matching funds for new or expanded initiatives drawn from the roughly 100 actions in Phase II of the County Climate Action Plan, spanning transportation, buildings and housing, energy use, and sustainable materials management. Applicants are encouraged to partner with neighbouring municipalities. The pilot round closed 17 June 2026.

applicant_notes.county: Monroe County is the funder, not an applicant.
applicant_notes.nonprofit: Not named as an eligible applicant; partner through a municipality.
applicant_notes.for_profit: Not eligible.
applicant_notes.individual: Not eligible.

geography.notes: Municipalities located within Monroe County only.

requirements: Project must map to an action in Monroe County Climate Action Plan Phase II
Matching funds required
Joint applications with neighbouring municipalities encouraged
grants.verification_note: Described as matching funds; the exact match ratio was not stated in the press release. 50% is an assumption flagged for correction. Pilot status means a second round is likely but unannounced.

grants.title: Rural Energy for America Program (REAP) — grant component
grants.summary: Renewable energy systems and energy efficiency improvements for agricultural producers and rural small businesses. Renewable energy grants are capped at $1 million per project and efficiency grants at $500,000. Cost share runs up to 25% of eligible costs on Farm Bill money and up to 50% on Inflation Reduction Act money. USDA paused acceptance of grant applications and announced in March 2026 that it will issue new regulations for the grant component; the guaranteed loan program remains open.

applicant_notes.individual: Agricultural producers with at least 50% of gross income from agriculture, including sole proprietors.
applicant_notes.for_profit: Rural small businesses meeting SBA size standards in an eligible rural area.
applicant_notes.nonprofit: Not eligible under this program.

geography.notes: Rural areas as defined by USDA. Agricultural producers may apply regardless of location; rural small businesses must be in an area under 50,000 population, which excludes the Rochester urbanized core.

requirements: Grant applications are not being accepted pending new regulations announced 31 March 2026
Guaranteed loan applications remain open
Applicants with a pending grant application may have to reapply
USDA has signalled tighter treatment of ground-mounted solar on productive farmland
grants.verification_note: The $2,500 floor comes from a secondary source. Award floor and the reopening date must be confirmed with the NY Rural Development State Energy Coordinator.

grants.title: Five Star and Urban Waters Restoration Grant Program
grants.summary: Modest grants to local partnerships improving water quality and the habitats that depend on it. Eligible work includes community tree canopy, community gardens, wetland, riparian and forest habitat restoration, and stormwater management, each paired with community outreach and stewardship. Roughly $2.5 million is distributed across 30 to 50 grants a year. The 2026 round closed in May with awards expected mid-to-late November 2026.

applicant_notes.individual: Not eligible; partner with a nonprofit or municipality.

geography.notes: National program. Great Lakes and urban watershed projects are competitive; the Genesee River and Irondequoit Creek watersheds fit the profile.

requirements: Minimum 1:1 match; matching contributions must be non-federal
Proposals must address at least one bullet under each of the five program priorities
Grants span roughly 12 to 18 months
grants.verification_note: Sources disagree on the award band: one reports $25,000-$50,000 with a $40,000 average, another $30,000-$60,000 averaging $45,000. The stored range is the union of both. One aggregator lists the next deadline as 16 May 2027 — confirm against the NFWF RFP when it posts. Tagged native_plants on the basis of the programme's pollinator and migratory bird habitat priority and its riparian/wetland restoration categories. Not an explicit native-species mandate.

grants.title: Composting and Food Waste Reduction (CFWR) Cooperative Agreements
grants.funder: USDA Office of Urban Agriculture and Innovative Production
grants.summary: Two-year cooperative agreements helping local and tribal governments and schools plan and implement municipal compost and food waste reduction programs. Priority goes to projects that make compost accessible to farmers and community gardeners, fold in food recovery, show economic benefit, and involve multiple partners. The programme has run on American Rescue Plan money since 2020; no FY2026 application round had been announced as of 1 August 2026.

applicant_notes.nonprofit: Eligibility for nonprofits varies by round; school districts and tribal governments have been named in past notices.
applicant_notes.state_agency: States have not been eligible recipients; advocacy groups have asked USDA to add them.
applicant_notes.for_profit: Not eligible.
applicant_notes.individual: Not eligible.

requirements: Projects must run two years
Multiple named project partners are expected
grants.verification_note: Last confirmed round was FY2024, which closed 4 September 2024. The programme depends on remaining ARPA funds and may not recur. Award range not published on the landing page — pull it from the Grants.gov notice if a new round posts. Tagged food_forest on the basis of the programme's stated interest in encouraging permaculture business development alongside composting. This is the only hook for perennial food systems anywhere in the current catalog.

grants.title: Water Quality Improvement Project (WQIP) Program
grants.summary: The state's main competitive grant for projects that directly cut water pollution — non-agricultural nonpoint source abatement, green infrastructure, salt storage, aquatic habitat restoration and municipal wastewater work. Runs through the Consolidated Funding Application, so it closed with the rest of the 2026 CFA round on 31 July. Awarded alongside the Non-Agricultural Nonpoint Source Planning grant and the newer Resilient Watersheds Grant, which together sent over $20 million to Genesee, Livingston, Monroe, Ontario, Steuben and Wayne counties in January 2026.

applicant_notes.nonprofit: Eligible for certain project categories in some rounds; confirm against the current RFA.
applicant_notes.for_profit: Not eligible.
applicant_notes.individual: Not eligible.

requirements: Applications accepted only through the Consolidated Funding Application
grants.verification_note: Programme existence, CFA routing and regional award history confirmed. Award range, match requirement and the 2026 category list were not confirmed — pull them from the WQIP RFA before entering figures.

grants.title: Environmental Justice Community Impact Grants
grants.summary: Grants of up to $200,000 to community-based organisations working on environmental and public health problems in their own neighbourhoods. Funded projects have included urban climate resilience and land-tending programmes, biodiversity restoration on vacant lots, and community-first environmental education. Six million dollars went to 32 organisations in April 2026; the next round has not been announced.

The most recent infrastructure round closed 27 February 2026.

grants.title: Forest Legacy Program - FY2028 Funding
grants.summary: The USDA Forest Service is requesting applications for the Forest Legacy Program (FLP), authorized by the Cooperative Forestry Assistance Act of 1978, as amended ( 16 U.S.C. 2103 ) and funded through the Land and Water Conservation Fund (LWCF). USDA Forest Service and States also cooperate with tribal and local governments, other Federal agencies, forest landowners, land trust organizations, and other partners to implement FLP.

grants.title: Cooperative Agreement for Affiliated Partner with the Great Lakes Northern Forest Cooperative Ecosystem Studies Unit (CESU)
grants.funder: Department of the Interior — Geological Survey
grants.summary: The U.S. Geological Survey's (USGS) Fort Collins Science Center is offering a cooperative-agreement funding opportunity to a CESU partner having capability to conduct research and studies related to the long-term demography of bumble bees, with a focus on imperiled species. The research will focus on Bombus affinis (rusty patched bumble bee), the previously-widespread bumble bee species whose populations have declined precipitously over the past two decades. This project will leverage collaborations to incorporate expertise in bumble bee ecology into a large existing project supporting the recovery of endangered and imperiled bumble bees.
